text: The Anchorline Systems deployment is picked, deployed, benchmarked, and tuned. The last skill in this capstone, and in the whole AI Infrastructure, ML Systems Engineer destination, is writing it up so someone who wasn't in the room can trust it and act on it. This lesson covers that write-up, then closes out the four-course arc that got you here.

A serving write-up earns trust by showing its work, in five sections. An executive summary — three sentences a manager will actually read. A methodology section with the model, the framework, the hardware, and the exact benchmark command, so the numbers are reproducible, not just quoted. A results section with the before-and-after table, numbers still hedged honestly where they're illustrative. And trade-offs and a recommendation, including what you rejected and why, and the open risk stated plainly rather than hidden.

Concretely: Mixtral 8x7B was considered and rejected for GPU budget, not quality. INT4 quantization was deferred, not dismissed — it's a lever still available if traffic grows. What shipped is Llama 3.1 8B on vLLM, a single 24 gigabyte GPU, tuned batching. And the open risk named outright: this is a single point of failure until autoscaling and load balancing from chapter five sit in front of it. A write-up that hides that risk is worse than no write-up at all.

Zooming all the way out: four courses, each adding one layer, nothing re-taught between them. GPU Computing gave you CUDA and the memory hierarchy. Distributed Training Infrastructure gave you the systems view of training at scale. ML Infrastructure and Platform Engineering gave you the platform a company builds once it has more than one model running. And Inference and Model Serving, this course, gave you the serving layer — now tuned and proven end to end in this very capstone.

That's the AI Infrastructure, ML Systems Engineer destination, complete — from raw hardware all the way to a benchmarked, defensible serving endpoint you can stand behind in a write-up. There's no next lesson here. There's a production system you now know how to build, measure, and defend.
